candidate_snippets.snippet: Executive Summary A regional fiber cut on 22 July disrupted connectivity between DC-North and DC-South, triggering cascading effects at both sites due to a shared authentication service that was, contrary to design intent, only deployed at DC-North without a local fallback at DC-South. This report documents both sites' timelines, impact, and root cause separately, since the two sites experienced different failure modes despite sharing a single triggering event.

The triggering event — a third-party fiber cut — was outside the organization's control and is not considered part of the root cause. The actual root cause is an architectural gap: the authentication service was designed to be deployed redundantly at both sites, per the original 2023 design document, but the DC-South deployment was deprioritized during the original rollout and never completed. This gap had not caused a visible incident before because DC-North and DC-South transport connectivity had not previously failed since the microwave backup link was commissioned two years ago. The delay between the fiber cut and traffic rerouting (14:02 to 14:34 at DC-South) was extended by the platform team's initial lack of awareness of the transport-layer event, since application monitoring and transport monitoring are currently on separate alerting systems with no cross-linking.
